A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bulwer-Lytton corpus study. Their complete main text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison; renamed datasets and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original humor-detector evaluations, literary-device analysis with human validation, and surprisal and adjective-noun analyses of human and generated sentences.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports surprisal distributions for GPT-4.1 and gpt-oss-120b in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The one-shot generation procedure, GPT-4.1 adaptation of TopicGPT, Gemma-based surprisal analysis, and Stanza/Infini-gram adjective-noun analysis are unchanged. The added explanation of structured outputs does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BL corpus, novel-opening and humor datasets, and sentences from four generators. 'crowd-first' becomes 'novel-openings'; Figure 9 analyzes existing generated corpora without adding a task, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 9 adds GPT-4.1 and gpt-oss-120b to the reported surprisal comparison alongside BL, GPT-5, and DeepSeek. These generators already appeared in v1's literary-device and adjective-noun comparisons. The humor detectors remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Generation settings, sampling, the Gemma model, the top-1000 token cutoff, rank normalization, and the human-annotation design are retained. The additional generator plots use the existing surprisal analysis without a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: New Figure 9 extends the analysis of how surprising tokens vary across sentence positions to GPT-4.1 and gpt-oss-120b. This adds evidence about generator-specific incongruity patterns. Existing genre breakdowns and feature-validation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averaging for humor detection, sentence-length standard deviations, surprisal-count dispersion, and annotator accuracy and agreement. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds two generator distributions, and Table 2 adds rare adjective-noun examples. Appendix C corrects the Purple Prose simile percentage from 84% to 78%, matching Figure 6's unchanged value of 0.78. Existing headline numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions of high-surprisal tokens, normalized ranks, and corpus-frequency-based adjective-noun novelty are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: Both claim a distinctive BL corpus, poor transfer of existing humor detectors, characteristic literary devices and adjective-noun combinations, and exaggerated stylistic features in generated sentences. The revised title and additional evidence do not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning incongruity and LLM exaggeration are retained. Limitations concerning subjective humor, detector coverage, labeling noise, minimal prompting, and the absence of human validation locating humor within sentences remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: The acknowledgments newly disclose Gemini and Claude Code assistance with experimental code and identify the annotators as Middlebury undergraduates. These are provenance disclosures; prompts, generation parameters, hardware, APIs, and code/data access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Taylor and Mazlack (2004) on wordplay recognition and Loakman et al. (2025) on LLM humor understanding. Section 3.2 newly positions its structured literary-device outputs against prior free-text humor explanations, without substantially reframing the work.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, renames 'crowd-first' to 'novel-openings,' makes localized prose edits, replaces one illustrative sentence in Appendix A, and renumbers appendices after moving dataset statistics. The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 move from appendices into the main text, Figure 9 is added, and existing plots receive sizing, label, and axis-formatting adjustments. These are localized presentation changes within the retained two-column design.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the 84%-versus-78% inconsistency, makes dataset statistics and illustrative results easier to find, and adds surprisal evidence for two existing generators. Clearer terminology and research positioning also help readers. These are modest gains in accuracy, accessibility, and evidential completeness; the central methods, findings, and limitations remain largely unchanged.
